claim:
Let \(\mathcal M=(M,\in)\) be a transitive set model of \(\mathrm{ZF}\), and let \(I
e\varnothing\). On the classical direct power \(M^I\), define \(f\in^*g\iff orall i\in I,\ f(i)\in g(i)\). Every equivalence relation compatible with \(\in^*\) is equality: if \(f
e g\), the coordinatewise singleton function \(s_f(i)=\{f(i)\}\) satisfies \(f\in^*s_f\) but \(g
otin^*s_f\). Consequently, when \(|I|\ge2\), the direct power's failure of extensionality cannot be repaired by any quotient that induces a well-defined membership relation.
integrity: The claim is supported by a symbolic proof for all functions in the stated domain; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof and no independent certification is claimed.
scientific_limitations: Assumes a transitive set model of ZF; no metatheoretic Choice is required.
Applies to the classical direct power with full function domain \(M^I\) and coordinatewise membership for nonempty \(I\).
Does not rule out other quotient or Boolean-valued semantic constructions.
The closest older direct-product thesis was not accessed in full text; independent audit has not been performed.
title: Congruence rigidity blocks quotient repair of classical set-theoretic direct powers
